Deadly flooding at the Grand Canyon threatens to cause economic damage, with a washed-out pipeline severing the South Rim's water supply and shutting down lodging at the popular tourist vista for an indefinite period.

The national park remains open but tourists who planned to stay overnight — many traveling long distances for reservations from a year or more ago — have had to scramble to find rooms elsewhere.

The flooding that killed two people and left a third missing washed out an already decrepit pipeline spanning the canyon that supplies every shower, faucet and spigot at the South Rim.

Now, hundreds of rooms are no longer available due to insufficient water, thwarting plans for thousands of tourists staying at the canyon or headed that way in the days ahead.

Michelle Allen, of Olathe, Kansas, got word Sunday evening she'd need to check out the next morning after just one night into a five-night stay.

“We had to hurry up and make accommodations somewhere else,” Allen said. “Luckily we were able to do that.”

Uncertainty ahead for residents, tourists and service workers

As of Tuesday, it's uncertain how long the area would be closed. Experts warn that the economic toll of such closures would affect not only northern Arizona but southern Nevada.

Many who visit the Grand Canyon also visit Las Vegas, said Christine Vogt, a consultant on sustainable tourism and outdoor recreation in the Western U.S.

“This will be catastrophic,” Vogt said, adding that the water shut-off could last weeks.

An extended lodging shutdown could also affect hundreds of service jobs in and around the national park and cost hundreds of thousands of dollars in local revenue, said Megha Budruk, an Arizona State University associate professor who studies communities near public lands.

The Grand Canyon weathered a fire last year, rain this year

This is the latest economic blow to the region after a wildfire last summer destroyed a historic lodge at the Grand Canyon's less busy but lusher North Rim, putting all rooms and cabins on that side of the canyon out of commission for over a year, with no date yet for getting them replaced.

In 2024, Grand Canyon National Park drew almost $1 billion a year in spending by close to 5 million tourists visiting the otherwise remote northern Arizona region, according to the National Park Service.

That spending further supported almost 9,000 jobs, which in turn generated $400 million in labor income and $1.1 billion in economic output in nearby communities, according to the park service.

Besides the shuttered Phantom Ranch lodge and campground at the canyon bottom directly affected by the floods, closed South Rim accommodations included El Tovar Hotel, Bright Angel Lodge, Maswik Lodge and the Yavapai Lodge and Trailer Village, park officials said.

South Rim campgrounds remained open but without spigots. Campground bathroom faucets would remain operational but campfires were banned since less water would be available to fight a wildfire.

An already dicey pipeline situation

Restaurants and other food and beverage services at the South Rim remain open. But only so much water will be available from tanks that were supplied by the cross-canyon pipe.

In all, some 2,000 year-round residents and the South Rim's millions of annual tourists rely on the 12.5-mile (20-kilometer) pipe built down, across and up the sheer canyon walls in the 1960s.

Grit in the water has scoured the aluminum pipe, weakening it from the inside and causing dozens of failures in recent years. A more than $200 million repair project was well underway before the flooding that had damaged about 40% of the pipeline.

Conservation will be at least part of the plan to keep water flowing from tanks that still have weeks' worth of water in them. After that, how the tanks might be refilled is an open question.

In the meantime, the priorities will be reporting leaks, using reclaimed water for nondrinking uses, running dishwashers and washing machines only if they're full or in eco mode, Xanterra spokesperson Stephanie Plieness said by email.

“And asking guests and staff to be mindful of things like handwashing length and running water,” Plieness said. “Actions like these across the South Rim are what’s helping the available water reserves go as far as possible.”

Some people move south to unaffected town outside the park

Unaffected was Tusayan, a tourism hub just outside the park boundary 15 minutes from the South Rim.

“We’re just heartbroken about what has happened at Phantom Ranch,” Tusayan Mayor Clarinda Vail said, adding: “We are open. Full services in Tusayan.”

The community with 1,200 lodging rooms doesn't rely on the pipeline but uses well water. Besides hotels and camping, Tusayan hosts restaurants and canyon ground and aircraft tour businesses.

At Grand Canyon Camper Village in Tusayan, business had been “oddly slow” for this time of year but now general manager Joan Marquez is seeing a surge in business at showers and laundry rooms. Both are available for the general public as well as people staying at the campground.

South Rim lodging companies such as Delaware North, which runs the 350-room Yavapai Lodge, promised to get as many customers rebooked in Tusayan as they could.

But the community’s five main hotels were filling up quickly. Grand Canyon Plaza Hotel is usually the last in town to sell out but was seeing a surge in South Rim lodgers seeking rooms, front desk supervisor Steven Ayres said.

“We’re going to have more coming, I guarantee you,” Ayres said.

___

Ty O'Neil at the South Rim contributed to this report. Gruver reported from Fort Collins, Colorado, and Yu from Phoenix, Arizona.

Authorities in Nepal mistakenly announced that a British aid worker had been rescued, confusing him with a survivor of the devastating flash floods that struck the country last week.

Former Gloucester councillor Alastair Chambers, 45, explained that the mix-up occurred when he arrived back in the capital, Kathmandu, on a humanitarian aid flight following volunteer work in a remote village.

Officials in Nepal had declared on Tuesday that a British national was rescued from the country's Rasuwa region.

In a Facebook statement, the Nepali Army confirmed that 119 people, among them a British citizen, were brought to safety through air operations.

However, Mr Chambers stated that he had travelled to the area specifically to assist with relief work and was never saved as part of any official rescue effort.

open image in gallery Mr Chambers flew to Nepal last week after seeing the devastation wreaked by the floods on the news ( AFP/Getty )

After spending several days in a village alongside the Trishuli river in central Nepal, he returned to Kathmandu aboard a humanitarian aid helicopter.

He said: “I got in the helicopter, the humanitarian aid helicopter, and I got dropped off at the army barracks, and when I got dropped off one of the police officers came up to me and asked for my details.

“Then they presumed that I’d been rescued. It’s been a bit of a weird one, really.

“I gave them my details, just abiding by the rules, and they obviously thought that I’d been rescued.

“News spreads – I was contacted by about 15 different journalists in the last few hours, just asking how I was and how I’m feeling after being rescued, and I had to say: ‘Well sorry, I haven’t been rescued.'”

“I thought they seemed very happy when I arrived,” he added.

Mr Chambers flew to Nepal last week after seeing the devastation wreaked by the floods on the news.

Together with other volunteers, he distributed sleeping bags, water purification tools, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges, travelling to the area by helicopter.

Mr Chambers said: “It’s quite dangerous, and we’ve got a lot of landslides, trees across the roads in front of us.

open image in gallery Mr Chambers distributed sleeping bags, water purification tools, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges ( AP )

“To take a journey that should take about one and a half hours, took about eight or nine hours in the end.

“We made our way there and then had a flood scare first thing in the morning.

“We’d been told that the floods were coming again… so we made our way up the mountain.

“Thankfully, it wasn’t large as the other torrent of water, so we waited until that settled and then made our way down and helped locate bodies and deliver humanitarian aid for the last few days.

“It’s been quite challenging, but it’s been very rewarding as well.”

Mr Chambers plans to fly back to the UK to raise money for the devastated village before returning with essentials and to set up solar powered lighting.

On Tuesday, Foreign Office minister Lord Wood of Anfield told the House of Lords that 36 British people are currently unaccounted for, up from the previous total of 33.

Minister for the Indo-Pacific, Baroness Winterton, will visit Nepal’s capital Kathmandu from Wednesday to Thursday to discuss support for recovery efforts, the Foreign Office said.

During her visit, Baroness Winterton will meet Nepali and UN officials, as well as embassy staff and members of the UK’s rapid deployment team, which is supporting the families of British nationals.

Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty will meet members of the British-Nepali community in London on Wednesday, to discuss the support available for those affected.

The UK Government has promised £5 million of humanitarian support support for relief and recovery efforts.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

Sports.title: Transfer deadline day LIVE: Man Utd's bombshell Ait-Nouri move, Enzo Fernandez imminent, Fofana twist
Sports.content:
Latest transfer news from Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and more as clubs in England and Wales have just a matter of hours to complete their summer business

Transfer deadline day: Five signings to watch out for

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer deadline day live blog, bringing you all of the latest news as clubs complete the mad dash to strengthen their squads.

Clubs in England and Wales have until 11pm tonight (Tuesday) to complete their business, although they are able to submit deal sheets before the deadline, which gives them an extra two hours to complete any late-night deals.

In terms of deals, what can we expect? Arsenal continue to be linked with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez, although it seems that the player is keen on a move to Barcelona.

Manchester City, meanwhile, have agreed a £125million move for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, who is en-route to undergo a medical with the Cityzens.

Liverpool are continuing to push for Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr, as a potential replacement for Cody Gakpo, who looks set to join Manchester City.

Manchester United could also look to complete a deal for a new left-back to compete with Luke Shaw. The club could also sanction the exit of striker Joshua Zirkzee.

As with most deadline days, there looks set to be some surprises along the way too. Make sure you stay with us for all of the latest.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona

Gabriel Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barcelona, where he's become their alternative to Julian Alvarez, after leaving Arsenal in a deal worth £12.85million

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus spoke honestly at his unveiling by Barcelona (Image: Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has admitted he isn't bothered about being Barcelona's second choice after Julian Alvarez following his transfer from Arsenal.

‌



Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barca, who agreed to pay the Gunners a fee which could reach £12.85million. The Brazilian entered the final year of his deal in north London and Mikel Arteta made it clear that he didn't feature in his plans for the 2026/27 season.

‌



He was frozen out of the first-team set-up along with Gabriel Martinelli and has now landed on his feet in Barcelona. The Catalan giants had wanted to sign Alvarez instead, but Atletico Madrid released a statement to publicly state they wouldn't do business with their La Liga rivals after growing irritated by their interest.

‌



Jesus rejected a move to Napoli and his decision ended up paying dividends, with a dream transfer to Barca the result. "A week ago I received a message that it could happen," he said at his unveiling. "When I started to think it was a real possibility, I was so excited. Now I can't wait to start training and playing.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list READ MORE :

"It doesn't annoy me [being Plan B to Alvarez], it doesn't bother me. What annoys me is if people say I'm a bad guy, which has never happened in my life - or if I am not playing football, that bothers me.

‌



"I have the chance to play for Barcelona, a chance I had 10 years ago and now life has offered me that opportunity again."

Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 for £45million, but his time in Arteta's side never really worked out. He slipped behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres in the pecking order and leaves having scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez looks set to stay at Atletico Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images)

‌



"I took a significant salary drop, but it's a dream to be here," Jesus added. "But it wasn't just me who had to make an effort to get the transfer over line, Barca also played their part.

"If you had asked me one month ago, I would have said it was unlikely this would happen. At 29, I didn't think I would have the chance to come to Barca."

He made 27 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal last season after recovering from a cruciate ligament knee injury. But after a summer of training he feels ready to hit the ground running for Hansi Flick's side, who needed a replacement for Robert Lewandowski.

Article continues below

"The last two years have been really complicated after the knee injury," Jesus said. "I was out of the game for almost one year, but it's in the past. I feel good physically now. I recovered well, returned to action for Arsenal and I am 100 per cent ready to play and give my all."

Sports.title: New Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki reveals reason he turned down Man Utd offer
Sports.content:
New Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki reveals reason he turned down Man Utd offer

Zion Suzuki has big boots to fill at Aston Villa after replacing Emiliano Martinez - three years after he turned down the chance of developing at Manchester United

View 2 Images Zion Suzuki made his Premier League debut for Aston Villa against Arsenal

Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki took the long road to the Premier League after turning down Manchester United.

‌



Suzuki, 24, admits he has got big shoes to fill after being brought in to replace Emiliano Martinez but the World Cup star is ready for the challenge.

‌



Japan No1 Suzuki snubbed a move to Old Trafford three years ago when United wanted to sign him to be understudy to Andre Onana. But Suzuki was brave enough to move from Urawa Red Diamonds to Belgian club Sint-Truiden because he wanted regular game time to help his progression.

‌



Within a year Suzuki had earned himself a move to Parma and he is now regarded as one of the best keepers in the world which is why Villa paid £30m for him this summer.

Suzuki said: “The priority was to play, that’s why I made the decision. I played in Belgium for one year and Parma for two years. I have been developing. It was very important to play in Serie A for two years. Now I am confident and I believe in myself.

‌

“I made good steps and now I am here to play for this club. I am enjoying this moment. I want to help the team as much as possible. In the end, I am here. I am playing for Villa. That’s it. I wanted to come here and now I just want to play for this club.”

Villa fans immediately sang “Zion Suzuki - the world’s No1” during his Villa Park debut against Arsenal on Monday night.

‌



That was what they used to chant at Martinez before his £7.5m switch to Chelsea and they were clearly determined to make Suzuki feel at home.

The Japan keeper shone at the World Cup before his nation were knocked out by Brazil but Suzuki admits following on from Martinez is a big ask. Their paths at Villa crossed over briefly before Martinez’s departure last week.

View 2 Images Suzuki said playing in the Champions League with Villa was a huge draw

‌



Suzuki said: “Yeah, of course there are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after him but I want to help the team and I want to be like him. It’s a good challenge for me.

“I trained with him a little bit. He is a good person and I learned from him. It was a short time but I did learn from him. I am looking forward to playing against him now.”

Suzuki says that he is now relishing the chance to play under Unai Emery and also in the Champions League for Villa. He is being encouraged to play out from the back which suits him even if Villa lost to Arsenal on his debut.

‌

“It was a difficult game. It was my debut but I wanted the win. We lost, so I am disappointed. But the manager said it is a process. We need to learn from defeats. Today we respected them but we lost and need to learn from this game and move forward.

Sports.title: Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list
Sports.content:
Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list

Chelsea are still in the hunt for a replacement as Manchester City attempt to sign Enzo Fernandez from the Blues and have identified five options

View 2 Images Chelsea are on the outlook for an Enzo Fernandez replacement (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Chelsea have a five-man shortlist to replace Enzo Fernandez on transfer deadline day that includes players from Arsenal and Tottenham. The Blues are working at finding a midfield signing who can arrive should the Argentina star leave Stamford Bridge in the coming hours.

‌



Fernandez could complete a momentous deadline day transfer to Manchester City before Tuesday's 11pm deadline, and become the first player to have commanded more than £100million twice.

‌



Chelsea's efforts so far have focused on landing Monaco ace Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Kone. They have so far been able to reach an agreement, with a £38.5m bid for Camara rejected, while Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini does not want Kone sold.

‌



Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Xabo Alonso has three more players on the club's shortlist, however, and all are closer to home. talkSPORT reports that Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi, Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall and Morgan Gibbs-White of Nottingham Forest are also under consideration.

Despite the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes to the Emirates this summer, Mikel Arteta suggested that Zubimendi was not available for sale. "No, he’s a really important player. He’s a really important player for us," Arteta said recently.

‌



"Zubi without a doubt was one of the best players for Arsenal last season. Without him we would never get into the position that we got in the last few weeks and he deserves massive credit.

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi is on Chelsea's shortlist (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Spurs ace Bergvall wanted to depart the club earlier in the transfer window but last week Roberto De Zerbi confirmed that he was also set to stay in north London. "Lucas Bergvall, 100 per cent," De Zerbi said when if his charge wanted to stay at Tottenham.

"We spoke a lot in pre-season. He's a top player, a top potential player. I like he stays, but I think now he wants to stay and we have no problem."

Gibbs-White, who is highly regarded by Chelsea, was set to move from the City Ground last summer but saw a transfer to Tottenham collapse when Nottingham Forest threatened legal action over their approach. Instead he signed a new deal with the Tricky Trees.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 23 deadline day signings ranked including Chelsea surprise and three record-breakers
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been busy this summer, but there could be more to come from the Gunners. Mikel Arteta has added nearly £200m worth of talent to his squad and might not be done just yet.

Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and Ezri Konsa have all joined for big money, with Hincapie joining after a year on loan. Links with Julian Alvarez aren't going away, while others continue to be linked during the dying embers of the window.

If there's more late business, it would be the 24th time Arsenal have made a deadline day signing since the transfer window system was introduced in 2002. That's not including those who initially joined the academy rather than the first team.

There's been a real mix, however, when it comes to whether those late arrivals succeeded or failed. We've ranked them from worst to best.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta cites Aston Villa moment as the inspiration behind Arsenal's win READ MORE :

23. Emiliano Viviano (Palermo, loan).

Italian goalkeeper Viviano arrived on a season-long deal from Palermo but didn't manage a single minute. Wojciech Szczesny and Lukasz Fabianski blocked his path and he quickly returned to his home country.

22. Cedric Soares ( Southampton, loan)

Cedric never looked like a great fit and Arsenal wasted little time seeking a better full-back option. Somehow stayed on the books for four years without ever threatening to be a regular.

21. Raheem Sterling (Chelsea, loan)

Sterling joined from Chelsea in a surprise switch but couldn't find his best form. A return of just one goal made this a calculated risk but one which didn't bear fruit.

‌



20. Kim Kallstrom (Spartak Moscow, loan)

Swedish midfielder Kallstrom was injured when he joined and only returned late in the season. Still, he enjoyed his time at the club and scored an emotional penalty in a cup semi-final shoot-out.

View 5 Images Kim Kallstrom's Arsenal spell was short-lived (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

This introductory offer saves £384 compared to the standard price, with every package also providing 100 regular channels alongside free Netflix and discovery+ subscriptions.

19. Andre Santos (Fenerbahce, £6m)

The Brazilian was a figure of fun at times but also earned cult hero status thanks to a goal against West Brom in May 2012. The effort was enough for Arsenal to clinch Champions League football at Tottenham's expense on the final day of the season.

‌



18. Lassana Diarra (Chelsea, £2m)

French midfielder Diarra had the opportunity to make an impression before departing. Arsenal turned a quick profit by sending him to Portsmouth but his success on the south coast may have had some wondering if he should have been given more time.

17. Julio Baptista (Real Madrid, loan)

The Brazilian forward joined via a loan exchange that saw Jose Antonio Reyes move to Madrid. He never really got going in the Premier League action but will be remembered for his part in a 6-3 League Cup victory over Liverpool.

16. Yossi Benayoun (Chelsea, loan)

Israel international Benayoun failed to secure a permanent switch after his loan spell. Enjoyed some encouraging moments, however, netting six goals across all competitions including four in the league.

15. Kieran Tierney (Celtic, £25m)

Scotland defender Tierney was great at times but injuries prevented him from making a greater mark in North London. Spent a year on loan in Spain and has now returned to Celtic.

‌



View 5 Images Injuries limited Kieran Tierney's involvement for Arsenal (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

14. Denilson (Sao Paulo, £3.4m)

Another Brazilian on the list, Denilson might have had more of an Arsenal career were it not for the emergence of Jack Wilshere. Made a real impact as a teenager in tough circumstances but eventually saw his time in England come to an end.

13. Takehiro Tomiyasu (Bologna, £16m)

The Japan international laid the framework for what a defender in a Mikel Arteta team looks like. He excelled when available but struggled with injuries and is now back in the Premier League with Crystal Palace after a stint at Ajax.

12. Jorginho (Chelsea, £12m)

Italy midfielder Jorginho helped Arsenal come close to the title in 2023 but the Gunners fell short. He was a big character off the field as well as on it.

‌



11. Thomas Partey (Atletico Madrid, £45m)

The Ghana midfielder was a big-money arrival from Atletico Madrid and had highs and lows on the pitch during his five years in England. Returned to La Liga with Villarreal in 2025 and is now in Saudi Arabia.

10. David Luiz (Chelsea, £8m)

View 5 Images David Luiz was one of a number of deadline day arrivals from Chelsea (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Yet another Brazilian, the centre-back played his part in the first trophy win under Arteta in 2020. Had some tough moments but showed his value on the pitch and in the dressing room.

9. Danny Welbeck (Man Utd, £16m)

A difficult departure for some United supporters and a well-received signing in North London. Was never prolific for Arsenal but delivered some big moments and is remembered fondly by a number of fans despite his numbers in front of goal.

‌



8. William Gallas (Chelsea, part-exchange)

The Gunners captain's behaviour at Birmingham in 2008 has overshadowed some of his better moments. However, there was good as well as bad after he arrived from Chelsea as part of the infamous Ashley Cole deal.

7. Andrei Arshavin (Zenit, £15m)

Signed a few months after impressing for Russia at Euro 2008 in what was then a record deal for Arsenal. Faded in his later years amid injury issues but will always have those four goals at Anfield.

6. Nacho Monreal (Malaga, £8.5m)

A bargain for a player who served the club admirably for the better part of a decade. Spain international Monreal became part of the furniture and played more for Arsenal than for any other club.

5. Piero Hincapie (Bayer Leverkusen, loan)

View 5 Images Arsenal continued their deadline day business by signing Piero Hincapie in 2025 (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



The Ecuador star has already done what he was signed for by helping Arsenal win the league, having done the same with Leverkusen. He could have a bigger role to play this term after joining permanently.

"When I spoke to Xabi just before we were going to sign him, I said if you have to describe him in one word, what would you use, and he said, 'He’s a warrior,'" Arteta told TNT Sports last season. "He will play through brick walls for you, and he’s one of the most competitive players that I have had.

4. Per Mertesacker (Werder Bremen, £8m)

A leader on and off the pitch. Mertesacker lifted Arsenal out of the doldrums in the latter half of the Arsene Wenger era and played a huge role after hanging up his boots.

In his role as academy manager, the German helped lay the groundwork for the likes of Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly to earn their place in the first team. There aren't many who have that kind of impact.

‌



3. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (Borussia Dortmund, £56m)

Another January deadline-day deal: Aubameyang followed his former Dortmund colleague Henrikh Mkhitaryan through the doors at Arsenal. The Gabonese international arrived in a club record deal and provided some star power.

The striker finished one season as the Premier League's top scorer and another as a cup winner after scoring both goals for Arteta's team in the final. The way things ended for him in North London shouldn't cloud that.

2. Mesut Ozil (Real Madrid, £42.5m)

The excitement around Arsenal when Ozil joined from Real Madrid will live long in the memory. The German creator was a really special player for a number of years, even if he couldn't help deliver a league title.

As with Aubameyang, the then-record signing left under a bit of a cloud. However, when he was good there were few in the league who could come close to him.

‌



1. Mikel Arteta ( Everton, £10m)

As with Mertesacker, Arteta's position is elevated by what came after he retired. What an impact, though.

There were plenty of positives on the field and in the dressing room, with Arteta providing leadership when it was needed most. Since he returned as manager, though, there has been so much more.

Sports.title: Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits embarrassing new low as viewers switch off
Sports.content:
Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits embarrassing new low as viewers switch off

Sky Sports News has come under fire for its deadline-day offerings, with misplaced musicians and rhyming reporters forcing fans to change channels

View 3 Images Sky Sports News' deadline coverage has been ripped apart by viewers online (Image: Sky Sports News)

Viewers have made their feelings crystal clear as Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits a "new low." An appearance by a guitarist and reporter Gary Cotterill's bemusing live dialogue have subscribers up in arms.

‌



Sky Sports News was once a non-negotiable on deadline day. Presenter Jim White, who left Sky in 2021, would front their live programme, in which he'd cut to roaming reporters at training grounds and stadiums while donning his revered yellow tie.

‌



Unforgettable moments, like drive-by interactions with former Tottenham, Portsmouth and QPR boss Harry Redknapp, Peter Odemwingie's faux pas and Arsenal fans losing their minds as Mesut Ozil's arrival was confirmed, were nearly guaranteed each year.

‌



But with the broadcaster undergoing a handful of changes, it appears as though the glory days have passed, and its restructured coverage has not landed well with subscribers to its channels.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA rules block Arsenal from Champions League clause as deadline day deal nears READ MORE :

As deadline day began on Tuesday morning, Sky Sports News enlisted the services of guitarist Ben Cipolla. Cipolla went viral during the World Cup with a song he wrote about England star Djed Spence, set to the tune of Bonnie Tyler's Total Eclipse of the Heart.

‌



Cipolla spoke to the channel's panel, including presenter Hayley McQueen and former Premier League striker Charlie Austin, before singing a new song about Liverpool recruit Bradley Barcola.

View 3 Images Cipolla's singing did not go down well (Image: Sky Sports News)

Barcola signed for the Reds on Monday in a blockbuster £123million deal from Paris Saint-Germain, and Cipolla commemorated the move with a song inspired by Crowded House's Don't Dream It's Over.

‌



It's safe to say those watching at around 8:30am were far from impressed. One claimed on social media platform X: "That channel has dropped right off a cliff."

Another concurred, writing: "Turned on Sky Sports News for transfer deadline and seen some p***k with a guitar. Turned it straight back off."

One more fan added: "Sky Sports News is one big joke these days. Deadline day used to be worth watching, but now it's just a gimmick." A fourth said: "Content from Sky Sports News hitting a new all-time low."

‌



But this song wasn't the only content that enraged subscribers. Cipolla also debuted another number about deadline day and some of the occasion's best moments. The lyrics included: "Deadline day is alive and kicking. So many deals, yeah, the clock is ticking."

In response to the song, a disgusted viewer wrote: "Genuinely the first time I've had to turn the television off out of pure second-hand embarrassment."

Reporter Cotterill, who was at Emirates Stadium on deadline day bringing fans updates about Arsenal's business, soon became the rotten cherry on top for some viewers.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Cotterill's antics were also criticised (Image: Getty)

When asked about any potential arrivals, Cotterill broke into song and, to the tune of Paul McCartney and Wings' Let 'Em In, sang: "No one's knocking at the door, no one's ringing the bell. No one's knocking at the door, no one's ringing the bell."

Cotterill then continued: "But then the fans are saying, 'If anybody does, open the door and let him in.'" One fan was particularly irked and wrote on X: "Who in their right mind would pay to watch that?"

Sports.title: Sheff Utd hit back to edge Bolton in five-goal thriller
Sports.content:
Romelle Donovan grabbed the winner in time added on to give Sheffield United a 3-2 victory over Bolton at Bramall Lane.

Xavier Simons struck inside the opening minute and Sam Dalby was also on target for the visitors, but United twice hit back to level with goals from Japhet Tanganga and Patrick Bamford before Donovan's dramatic goal secured all three points for Chris Wilder's men.

The visitors got off to a flying start, scoring with only 23 seconds on the clock. Thierry Gale broke down the left and advanced into the area before firing in a shot which was blocked, with Simons seizing on the rebound and hooking the ball into the net.

United responded soon afterwards, levelling in the fourth minute when Sydie Peck's free kick was met by Tanganga, whose far-post header crept just inside Jack Bonham's right-hand post.

That set the tone for the rest of the half with the home side dominating and going close to taking the lead on several occasions.

Chris Forino came to Bolton's rescue when Bamford looked set to score, producing a superb goal-line clearance to keep the striker's shot out.

Bamford also failed to get a proper connection to a low cross from Ben Brereton-Diaz, screwing his shot wide, while Peck's shot fizzed over the bar and Donovan fired off target.

Bolton went close soon after the re-start when Gale's low shot was touched wide by Michael Cooper. John McAtee also had a chance to put them back in front, shooting a fraction wide.

The visitors regained the lead in the 67th minute when Gale's cross from the left found Dalby, who planted a header past Cooper after getting between two defenders.

Bamford made it 2-2 a minute later, stabbing in from close range after Sam McCallum did well on the left and played the ball across the face of goal.

The home side rode their luck at times with Cooper kept busy as Bolton enjoyed a good spell.

It took an important save from Cooper to keep the scores level, turning McAtee's downward header onto the bar. The keeper also got down smartly to his left to keep out Josh Sheehan's firm drive and then did well to tip over Samuel Iling-Junior's effort from inside the area.

Then, in the third minute of time added on, a ball from Kalvin Phillips picked out Donovan, who strode into the area before beating Bonham with a shot which struck the roof of the net.

Sports.title: Bristol City win piles more misery on struggling Preston
Sports.content:
Two late goals helped Bristol City secure back-to-back Championship wins as they saw off spirited Preston 3-1 at Deepdale.

Scott Twine had tapped City into a fourth-minute lead but the Lilywhites fought back strongly and Caleb Wiley slammed them level with a 51st-minute rocket.

Lisav Eissat's looping 79th-minute header crushed North End hearts before Dom Ballard coolly bagged his second goal of the season, albeit less spectacularly than his stunner against Birmingham, to secure the victory seven minutes later.

The night started woefully for the hosts as Lorent Tolaj picked out Twine with an inviting centre and the ex-Burnley man gobbled up from close range with a first-time finish.

Despite the shocking start, North End should have levelled minutes later as Jusef Erabi failed to properly connect with Liam Lindsay's inch-perfect delivery with the goal gaping.

The hosts continued to take the game to their opponents and went close twice in quick succession as Sam Tickle did well to turn Jordan Thompson's free-kick over the bar before Delano Burgzorg beat the 24-year-old with a header across the goal from Harry Clarke's cross, only to be denied by the foot of a post.

Those early chances seemed to wake the Robins up and former Preston loanee Sam Greenwood stung the palms of Daniel Iversen with a 25th-minute snapshot from the edge of the box having been teed up by Twine.

Nonetheless, an all-action Thompson was trying his best to drag his side level, thundering a 30-yard howitzer narrowly over the bar in the 35th minute while Greenwood again fired straight into Iversen's hands.

Wind kept very much in the sails of Paul Heckingbottom's men after the break and they could have scored twice before they did, Clarke heading Thompson's corner wide from close range and then through Alfie Devine, who failed on several occasions to pull the trigger in the box before eventually being blocked by Tickle.

But that pressure eventually did pay dividends as Wiley caught everybody by surprise with a sensational drive from range that nestled into the corner.

Preston fans were even more buoyant on the 68th minute as a big screen announcement confirmed they had signed two new players on deadline day but that euphoria almost turned sour within a minute as Tolaj broke clear on goal, only for Iversen's leg to keep out his effort.

Michael Skubala's team were steadily growing back into the game and killed Preston off with two late sucker punches.

Eissat expertly looped Rio Cardines' free-kick out of Iversen's reach to put his team ahead and Ballard pounced on some suspect defending to round the goalkeeper and score a third, condemning Preston to a fourth straight loss.

Sports.title: West Ham beat Wolves to claim first league win of the season
Sports.content:
Divine Mukasa scored twice as West Ham beat Wolves 4-2 to pick up their first three points since last season's relegation to the Championship.

Wolves, who also went down from the Premier League last term, could have gone top with a victory but ended up losing for the first time under new manager Cesar Peixoto.

Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also scored for the hosts, with Marshall Munetsi and Mavropanos' own goal replying for Wolves.

The win eased the pressure on manager Nuno Espirito Santo on a night when Amanda Staveley, who is heading a consortium looking to buy a significant stake in West Ham, was at the London Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player West Ham's Divine Mukasa scores a 25-yard screamer to put West Ham in the lead against Wolves.

West Ham struggled initially and were relieved when Raul Jimenez, picked out in space in the box by Jackson Tchatchoua, shanked wildly wide.

Jimenez's next attempt, from a corner played almost to the edge of the box, was better though. The Mexico striker's shot bounced off the turf, over goalkeeper Mads Hermansen and on to the top of the crossbar.

Mateus Mane also hit the bar not long afterwards, from the left of the box after Kyle Walker-Peters had failed to cut out a cross. The full-back recovered to get just enough of a deflection on the shot that followed.

A goal was coming and it was the hosts who scored it against the run of play in the 33rd minute.

Mukasa, the on-loan Manchester City midfielder, unleashed a rising drive from more than 20 yards that went in off the underside of the crossbar.

West Ham were a team transformed, with Munetsi having to block on the line from Max Kilman.

And they were awarded a penalty in the 40th minute for Andre's lunge on Joel Piroe. Bowen sent goalkeeper Jose Sa the wrong way to slot home.

Wolves hit back in the 43rd minute when Munetsi won a chase with Mavropanos that saw him turn the Greek defender and end a low drive beyond Hermansen's dive to his left.

West Ham increased their lead in the 53rd minute through Mukasa. The teenager accepted Bowen's pass from the right and saw his shot loop off the boot of Nasser Djiga to leave Sa helpless again.

Sa batted away a Bowen drive from an angle but West Ham made it 4-1 in the 64th minute through Mavropanos' goal from the resulting corner. The centre-back saw his header deflected on to the crossbar but lashed home the rebound, also off the bar.

Wolves pulled a goal back in the 69th minute when Mavropanos, sliding in to stop Tchatchoua setting up substitute Jordan James, diverted the ball into his own net.

Sports.title: In-form Swansea ease past Watford
Sports.content:
Swansea moved top of the Sky Bet Championship with a 2-0 home win over Watford.

Adam Idah and Eom Ji-sung grabbed first-half goals as Swansea made it 10 points from four games, leapfrogging Charlton and Wolves to take over at the summit.

It also meant Watford lost their unbeaten league record after beating Southampton and drawing against Wrexham and West Ham.

Watford showed plenty of intent throughout but were unable to remedy the situation after a difficult opening half-hour in which Swansea oozed confidence and class.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joseph Opoku missed a great opportunity to put Swansea ahead against Watford after a hectic goalmouth scramble

Before kick-off paid Swansea tribute to their former manager Kenny Jackett, who died in June at the age of 64.

Jackett spent his entire playing career at Watford with 428 appearances for the Hornets and his family were in attendance at Swansea.com Stadium.

Swansea were impressive from the off, with Idah testing Federico Ravaglia and Marko Stamenic heading against a post, with Joseph Opoku unable to force the ball home in a desperate scramble almost on the goal-line.

The visitors' defence was breached after eight minutes when Stephen Eustaquio, on his home debut after arriving from Porto, released Idah and he had presence of mind to give Eom a tap-in for his second goal in as many games.

Watford cleared their heads for Mattie Pollock and Hector Kyprianou to go close, but Swansea doubled their advantage after 29 minutes.

This time Eom was the creator, cutting in from the left-hand touchline and finding Idah with a delicious reverse pass.

Idah steadied himself as Ravaglia approached and slipped the ball through the goalkeeper's legs with the minimum of fuss.

Watford hinted at a way back into the contest as Mamadou Doumbia sent a header over and Kyprianou did not get enough purchase on his, and the Hornets also started the second half well.

Swansea should have extended their lead when Melker Wildell fed Eom, but this time the South Korean lacked conviction and Ravaglia rushed out to avert the danger.

Idah's work-rate was to be admired and the Republic of Ireland striker left the action midway through the second period to a rousing ovation.

Zan Vipotnik replaced Idah, with last season's Championship top scorer seemingly set to stay at Swansea after summer speculation that he was to leave the club.

Wildell whistled a shot past a post, while Edoardo Bove led a Hornets' breakout at the other end for Edo Kayembe to blaze over.

The cherry on the Swansea cake was almost applied 10 minutes from time after more slick passing from Vitor Matos' side found Wildell in a central position 20 yards out.

Wildell's ferocious strike seemed to be arrowing in, but Ravaglia stuck out a strong right hand to deny the Sweden international his first Swansea goal.

Sports.title: Chelsea agree £47m deal to sign Monaco's Camara
Sports.content:
Chelsea have agreed a £47m deal to sign Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

He is set to sign a six-year deal pending a medical. Monaco rejected a £38.5m (€45m) bid from Chelsea earlier on Deadline Day.

Chelsea are looking for a new midfielder with Enzo Fernandez set to depart for Manchester City in a joint-British-record £125m deal.

Roma's Manu Kone was also shortlisted as a potential option, while Chelsea are also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

Camara has spent the last two years at Monaco having joined from Metz in 2024.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes the signing of Enzo Fernandez will make Manchester City the biggest challenge to Arsenal in the race for the Premier League title.

Manchester City have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m.

The deal matches the British record transfer fee Liverpool paid for Newcastle striker Alexander Isak during last year's summer Deadline Day.

Chelsea will make a £18m profit on the midfielder they signed for £107m three-and-a-half years ago.

Who has left Chelsea on Deadline Day?

Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como.

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg. Essugo was of interest to Hull in this window.

Striker Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to Strasbourg. He signed from Santos for £17.1m three years ago but made only three appearances.

Forward Dujuan Richards has also joined Wimbledon on a season-long loan.

Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow ahead of his loan move to Celtic, who are also working to finalise a deal for Chelsea left-back Landon Emenalo.

Spurs pivoted to Ukraine international Mudryk on Monday after a dramatic finale to a remarkable summer transfer window for the north London club. After no progress in a pursuit for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo, Tottenham reached an agreement in principle with Everton for Iliman Ndiaye on Sunday before Manchester City, having also missed out on Gakpo, hijacked the deal, forcing De Zerbi to turn to Mudryk. Mudryk returned from a 20-month suspension last month and worked with De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk before a transfer to Chelsea in 2023. It has been a difficult time for the 25-year-old after he was banned in 2024 by the Football Association due to an “adverse finding” for meldonium. However, Mudryk will aim to rediscover his best form under De Zerbi on a season-long loan that includes a £75m option to buy. Speaking during Tottenham’s pre-season tour of Australia when Mudryk’s ban ended, De Zerbi said: “He’s my son. I’m very happy. He deserves to play. He’s a cool guy, a top player.
