Sports.title: ‘In my heart until I die’: Argentina says a tearful thank you to Lionel Messi
Sports.content:
Anyone who was present at Lionel Scaloni’s press conference immediately after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey on 19 July and saw his tears, the sobs which prevented him from speaking while he got up and walked out, could tell this was a man weeping not because of defeat in a single match but because he was fully aware that what that particular group of men had been through for the past eight years had come to an end.

Messi’s announcement that he is retiring from international football, posted on Instagram on Monday complete with photos of three handwritten sheets of some anonymous yet corporate-looking headed paper and a Harry Potter Time Turner pen, to the soundtrack of Brindis sung by Soledad Pastorutti, instantly dominated the news and unleashed a barrage of homages, gratitude and joy from all corners. But it’s not exactly a surprise.

“How crazy that the day has come, dear Leo,” Cristian Romero posted, making it clear that this was expected in spite of the unexpectedness. “The day no one wanted to arrive has arrived,” echoed Giovani Lo Celso, who said he had “nine years listening to you, admiring you and learning by your side”. His international teammates highlight how in their childhood they dreamed of meeting him one day, let alone actually playing with him. Nico Paz says since he was four years old he “used to watch you play with my dad and we would calculate together whether I would be in time to play with you”.

It’s not just his teammates who are expressing gratitude and nostalgia. On a Buenos Aires street corner someone put a red telephone on a table with a sign saying: “What would you say to Messi?” Passersby picked up the receiver and talked into it: “I’m 86 years old and you have given me the greatest joys in my life. You will be in my heart until the day I die,” one gentleman said. A young boy saw the news and “burst into tears even though I was at school”. A well-spoken woman said “we will miss you because you are an extraordinary being”, a little girl added “you’re the best and the greatest”. An old man signed off “bye, son”.

Influencers, journalists, artists, cultural commentators and psychologists all expressed their gratefulness for Messi being a great human being. “Messi led by example,” the veteran sportswriter Matías Martin wrote, while the coach and motivational speaker Matias “Coco” Gallo Bevegni posted that the World Cup winner “taught me more in defeat than in victory”.

View image in fullscreen A message written by Lionel Messi and posted to Instagram explaining his retirement from the Argentina team. Photograph: Lionel Messi/Instagram/Reuters

The football pundit Morena Beltrán could not hold back the tears as she explained to her older colleagues that for her generation there is a sense of mourning and emptiness which can only be filled by gratitude, which maybe they have already experienced, because they have seen another God. The psychoanalyst Milagros Filgueras praised the decision to hand-write the note, saying some goodbyes need the body involved. The journalist Pablo Perantuono devoted his column to the “epistolary genre”, noting that a handwritten letter in this day and age is almost a countercultural act of originality.

The writer Andrés Burgo highlighted that in 10 of the past 12 World Cups, either Maradona or Messi played, so this truly marks the “end of an era in which grandparents, parents, sons and daughters and grandchildren enjoyed an incredible privilege during almost 45 years. The heir will arrive – we hope – but right now is a time of orphanage. And gratitude.”

View image in fullscreen Argentina fans wearing T-shirts depicting Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona. Photograph: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Messi revealed that this letter was actually written two days after the final, a cathartic diary-like release, but that on Monday, after “[what happened with] my dad” he was more convinced than ever. The note said: “It’s a decision that hurt and continues to hurt,” but that he understands this is the moment. The poet Valeria Correa Fiz pointed out that he originally wrote “I think”, crossed it out and replaced it with “I understand”. Messi swore he always gave his all, not only these past few years when “everything was won” (he never says “I won”; it’s always “we” or “it” was won) but he has nothing left to give. He’s emptied.

The 39-year-old, however, scored four goals for Inter Miami at the weekend and continues his career at club level, where he clearly still has much to give. He is not retiring from playing football, the thing he loves most. He is retiring from Argentina.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Messi shows off the World Cup trophy after winning the 2022 final against France. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

With two international dates coming up and no rival agreed, no doubt the clarification that there will be no Messi in the squad will impact on the potential fixtures. And not unlike the time when he quit Argentina before, in 2016, the country’s football is in a bit of turmoil.

The context and climate include scandals surrounding the Argentinian Football Association, the pressure by some lobbies to privatise football clubs, which are non-profit organisations, and the international furore caused by several incidents during the World Cup which have landed Argentina with some hefty fines, sanctions and suspensions.

The heaviness of the Argentina flag which for so many years visibly weighed him down, turned idyllic when it became the cloak of victory, mattered very much to his father, Jorge. Messi said he wanted to win another World Cup for him. Perhaps his death has somehow freed him from that aspect of his Argentinianness.

View image in fullscreen Supporters in Sydney, Australia, watch Messi on giant TV screens after Spain defeated Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final. Photograph: David Gray/AFP/Getty Images

And just like last time, the spontaneous visceral response from the Argentinian people is acceptance and relish at the good times lived. That inexplicable sense of pride that comes from being from the same soil as someone who is very good at something and whose magic is still untarnished by the sordid final match against Spain, or any of the criticisms directed at the squad and fans throughout the tournament. If anything, his final tears in front of the stands, like Scaloni’s tears at the press conference, are mirrored in a nation moved profoundly by the generations we have just lived through, perhaps not realising we were living through them.

The huge volume of emotive, sentimental outpouring is rather lovely, and amid it all an enduring image of three little boys walking down a Buenos Aires street with No 10 Messi shirts on their backs signals the way forward, towards a future unknown.

Sports.title: Aston Villa sign Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis as Newcastle get Fernandez-Pardo
Sports.content:
Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.



The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started May’s Europa League triumph in Istanbul; Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.



Watkins’ £50m exit to Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.



After Monday’s 1-0 home defeat to Arsenal, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” said Villa’s manager. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”



Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages. “In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.



“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that, I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”

Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window that has also seen Eddie Howe replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” said Wilson. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo is seen as having the ability and verstatilty to be an ideal fit for Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle. Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” acknowledged Wilson. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

“I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club,” said the Belgian. “I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”

Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high intensity gameplans explains why Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two different clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.

Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool, while across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.

Kevin Danso has joined Sunderland on a year-long loan from Tottenham that should lead to a formal £25m transfer for the Austria centre-half next summer.

Fulham have completed the signing of Manuel Ángel from Real Madrid, having already signed César Palacios and Gonzalo García from the Spanish giants.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Tottenham and the rapid disappearance of their club hype man
Sports.content:
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Before we get going, a reminder to join our team of writers for all the latest transfer deadline day updates before the window slams shut (in most major leagues) at 11pm BST. Get on it.

NOT SO HOT(SPURS)

While Football Daily isn’t going to claim to have looked too hard, the earliest mention we could find of Tottenham Hotspur being “in very real danger” of having to play Lincoln City home and away this season dates back to early March. Thomas Frank had been sacked a couple of weeks previously and fabled firefighter Igor Tudor had arrived in north London, only to lose his first two matches. While the weird but mercifully brief fever dream prompted a deluge of further hand-wringing, Spurs eventually avoided the drop thanks to replacing the Croat with Roberto De Zerbi. A more passable version of Red Adair, the Italian masterminded heroic wins over already-relegated Wolves, a Villa side focused entirely on Bigger Vase and an Everton team who had last done anything of interest 31 years previously. Not so much a miraculous escape, as a quite fortunate one aided by the benevolence of the fixture generator, it prompted the club hierarchy to hose cash in all directions, all the better to ensure Spurs never find themselves circling the drain again.

So how’s that going, eh? Just two top-flight games into the new campaign and De Zerbi’s much-bolstered squad is already rock bottom of the table and six points off the early pace set by their relegation rivals Hull City. And having completely embarrassed themselves at Brentford on the opening weekend of the season, you could have been forgiven for presuming their first home game of the campaign might have been prefaced by a modicum of humility. Eh? Eh? Oh. “We’ve spent and we’ve spent and we’ve spent!” whooped the designated club hype man in his pre-match address from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium sward, a field of nightmares upon which Beyoncé has played twice as many gigs as the three league wins Spurs managed last season. “We’re back! We’re going places! We’re huge!”

Approximately 90 minutes and a third consecutive home defeat at the hands of Newcastle later, there was scarcely a peep from said hype bro, so loud was the jeering of Geordies revelling in the obvious discomfort of their former midfielder Sandro Tonali, who could scarcely have done less to justify his £100m summer fee before being hooked in raucous ignominy. “Forget the result,” cooed De Zerbi, after witnessing his side go down to goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa. “I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result. There is no panic. I know where we are going and what the plan is.” Of course everyone has a plan until they get the kind of smacks in the face dished out by Brentford and Newcastle but De Zerbi can at least take heart from the fact that on Saturday, Tottenham looked pretty impressive until they didn’t. It’s a minor victory that will have to do until obliging Everton come to town in two games’ time.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Now on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, all the lesser disgraces.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It is a decision that hurts my soul but I know it is time. I love, have loved and I will always love being part of the national team. I have emptied myself: now I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are great young players coming through who deserve to be [selected]. I love you! I thank God for making me Argentinian” – Lionel Messi, with the heaviest of hearts, bids farewell to international duty.

View image in fullscreen An artist draws a painting of Lionel Messi, in Mumbai. We can’t draw for toffee so we’re in no position to criticise the likeness. Photograph: Divyakant Solanki/EPA

double quotation mark As probably the greatest player in history has announced his retirement from international football, I’d like to do likewise. Sure, the ingrates never picked me, overlooking my abilities through several World Cups and Euros, but I feel that, like Messi, the time has come to finally hang up my … ah, hopes of a call-up. But never say never, eh? Look all that happened when the little maestro changed his mind last time around! So, yes, I could still be talked out of this decision, should my country decide they need me. Thank you and …goodbye. For now, at least” – Justin Kavanagh.

double quotation mark Early days but Emi Martínez’s transfer for £7.5m seems like the bargain of the season. OK, he let in three against Brighton but saved many more and transformed Chelsea’s defence. I wonder how much they could sell Robert Sánchez on for? I predict, probably much more than £7.5m” – Nigel Sanders.

double quotation mark So August has just ended and my household is already in a contest to see ‘who can have the most miserable season’, which should cheer up anyone whose pre-season optimism has had an early blow. Me: Luton – one win from three in League One with 10 goals conceded. My wife and son: Spurs – say no more. My other son: West Ham – one win from three in the Championship. It’s going to be a long nine months” – Kevin Goddard.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Justin Kavanagh. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Barcelona breeze past Rayo but all eyes in Spain remain on Julián Álvarez
Sports.content:
If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian’s two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix – impressive again in his link-up play – and you have a fluid, fearsome front three.

Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one – at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. “He’s a top striker,” the coach said. But Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez is the ultimate prize.

While Mikel Arteta has apparently attempted to speed up a possible deal with a phone call to Álvarez, the Barcelona president, Joan Laporta, has conducted his interest largely in public. He stirred the pot again last Wednesday after Arsenal’s interest was firmed up. “This whole situation has created a lot of noise,” said Laporta, who specialises in creating a lot of noise, in a video on Barça’s social channels. “Atlético told us they were not selling [Alvarez]. However, it looks like, from what we hear now, they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.”

Laporta left little to the imagination: “We are very interested in buying Julián Álvarez. We would like our offer to be accepted.” Atlético are not playing ball – and who can blame them? Barcelona’s courting of Antoine Griezmann, who announced he was staying at Atlético in a TV documentary in 2018 only to move to the Camp Nou in 2019, still leaves a sour taste. Again they have shown disapproval at Barcelona’s behaviour in their pursuit of Álvarez. “This situation isn’t about money, it’s about dignity,” an embattled Atlético said in a statement the day after Laporta’s video message.

After the hostile reception he received from Atlético’s fans at the Metropolitano when coming on as a substitute against Villarreal the previous weekend, Álvarez missed some training sessions and the 3-1 win at Sevilla on Saturday. Atlético said the striker was unwell. He returned to training on Sunday, with Arsenal appearing his only route out by the end of Tuesday – “there is zero consideration of an Álvarez transfer to Barcelona,” Atlético said.

Álvarez’s absence was felt keenly at the Camp Nou on Monday – for about 20 minutes. After some sloppy Barcelona finishing and an emphatic strike from Rayo’s Sergio Camello, a striker who came through Atlético’s academy, the headlines were obvious. But the narrative did not come to the rescue of the Rayo centre-back Pathé Ciss, who ended up on his backside after Raphinha skipped past him and slotted in the equaliser.

View image in fullscreen Gabriel Jesus gestures upon arrival at the airport in Barcelona on Monday. Photograph: Enric Fontcuberta/EPA

On an evening when Argentina’s footballers were writing Instagram posts about international retiree Lionel Messi, Barcelona’s current No 10 paid tribute in his own way. Lamine Yamal cut inside and whipped a shot past the flying Dani Cárdenas, high at his near post, to establish a lead that was never surrendered. After rumours about the 19-year-old’s fitness and wellbeing circulated following his sluggish start to the season, Flick reminded everyone that the kid had only three weeks’ holiday since beating Messi and Argentina in the World Cup final. Lamine Yamal was reaching his “top level” in training, Flick insisted, and it was hard to argue with him.

It was also hard to argue with Florian Lejeune when the Rayo defender said in a half-time interview that Barcelona “are very good”. Six minutes after the restart, he turned the ball into his own net. Gordon, the most expensive outlay at the Camp Nou this summer except perhaps for the new roof that is still under construction, provided the cross for that own goal and a great deal more from the left wing. The England forward’s selfless passing and running has quickly endeared him to supporters and there were chants of “Gordon, Gordon, Gordon” from behind the goal. His backheel set up Raphinha’s second and Barça’s fourth to make it three assists in three games.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona’s fourth goal with Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Lluís Gené/AFP/Getty Images

After an hour of chasing Pedri, Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal, Rayo’s midfield had to contend with Rodri off the bench. The marquee arrival from Manchester City did not have the chance to parade the World Cup he had won as Spain’s captain before his Barcelona debut in the win against Athletic last Thursday. Barça snubbed the trophy presentation following a row over the arrest of one of their supporters who was carrying an Estelada flag – a symbol of the Catalan independence movement – outside the stadium before their season opener at Elche. Athletic’s Spain players had faced whistles from some Basque fans when they presented the trophy in Bilbao. Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella and Real Sociedad’s Mikel Oyarzabal were given a warm reception at the Bernabéu last week.

Lamine Yamal’s second against Rayo, another Messi-esque finish from the edge of the box, put the result beyond doubt. Barcelona and Real Madrid – the only teams with 100% records after three games – are yet to blink as the title race begins, but all eyes on transfer deadline day, you expect, will be on the exit door at Atlético’s training ground.

Talking points

While Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé were on the scoresheet in Real Madrid’s 4-0 home win against Málaga, it was the performance of Trent Alexander-Arnold that was perhaps most striking. The former Liverpool right-back was a creative force, setting up Madrid’s third for Mbappé, in his first start under José Mourinho. Mbappé, tipped for the Ballon d’Or by Mourinho last week, topped the scoring charts for a day or so after his sweeping finish from Alexander-Arnold’s low cross.

Quick Guide La Liga results Show Racing Santander 3-2 Elche, Alavés 1-0 Villarreal, Levante 5-2 Real Betis, Real Sociedad 2-1 Espanyol, Sevilla 1-3 Atlético, Real Madrid 4-0 Málaga, Deportivo La Coruña 3-1 Valencia, Celta Vigo 0-2 Athletic, Barcelona 5-2 Rayo Vallecano, Osasuna 1-0 Getafe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Aside from Mbappé the most in-form striker in La Liga might be Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. The 37-year-old scored for the third game in a row as Deportivo beat Valencia 3-1 at Riazor for their first top-flight victory since 2018. Aubameyang could not suppress a giggle at the mention of Adama Traoré in a post-match chat with the media – his former Barcelona teammate has just signed from West Ham: “I’ve told him: ‘We are waiting for you.’”

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang finds the net again for Deportivo. Photograph: Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images

Despite competition from Deportivo’s Bright Ede, who crossed the ball into his own box for Valencia to score, defensive mishap of the weekend goes to Matías Dituro. The 39-year-old Elche goalkeeper tried to juggle the ball into his own penalty area to pick it up but was beaten to it by Levante’s Yassir Zabiri, who poked in the first of a hat-trick in Racing Santander’s first win in primera since 2012. “Matías is a very daring goalkeeper. We had spoken to Yassir: I thought he could win the ball off him – and look how it turned out,” said Racing’s prophetic head coach, José Alberto.

Sports.title: ‘I was scared to tell my old teammates’: Victoria Pelova on making leap from Arsenal to Spurs
Sports.content:
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women’s teams as there is between their men’s counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.

Victoria Pelova’s move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well wishes and love.

“I was really scared to tell my old teammates that I was going here,” Pelova says. “My close friends knew about it, obviously, but everyone responded so well. Everyone tells me that it reflects on the person I am. So, I’m actually really glad about that.”

Pelova has been an Arsenal fan favourite despite limited minutes in her three years at the club, during which she was hampered by an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained on international duty in June 2024. Why is she so liked? She comes across as fun and is loved by her teammates, with a wicked and dry sense of humour.

Pelova was not worried what people would make of her move to Spurs, but the Netherlands midfielder did think about it. Ultimately, it was “an easy decision” to join Martin Ho’s squad.

“The way Martin approached me, what he said about how he sees me as a player, the videos he showed me and how he wants me to be, I’ve actually never had a coach talking like that about me. So, for me, it was a good decision. I talked a lot with my mum about it and she immediately said yes. That was actually the most important thing for me, what my mum thought.”

At the start of June, Pelova shared online that her mum had died. A carousel of moving photos of the pair through the years was captioned: “Your biggest fear was leaving me behind. My biggest fear was losing you. Rest now, Mum.”

Pelova is not ready to talk about the loss, but it sits in the background of the interview. Not having to move home as a result of her leaving Arsenal was important. “It does really help me that I have friends and family around me that take care of me,” she says.

View image in fullscreen Pelova slides in on Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson during Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in January. Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty Images

Reflecting on her spell at Arsenal, with her ACL injury coming at a time when it was believed she would start to get more playing time, she says: “There was a private situation going on, my mum was ill, and I didn’t get minutes. So, it was a really tough time and people didn’t know what I was going through.”

The goal now? “To be happy again, in football and outside football, and just day by day see how it goes.

“It sounds like I have not been happy, but I have been happy in the last year and in being with my friends. But when you’re not playing as regularly as you want to it’s inevitable that you’re not going to be totally happy, and when I’m the happiest person, I will be the best footballer I can be.”

The fresh start at Tottenham has been rejuvenating. “It’s nice to have no one know you. For me, that’s the way to go. I don’t know if I can explain it, but I feel like when everyone knows you, they focus on the things they know.”

Ho made an instant impression on Pelova. “All the coaches I’ve met are always like: ‘Oh, you can play there and there and there.’ Martin was like: ‘You’re this for me.’ He knew exactly where he wanted me and what he wanted from me. That, right away, set the tone for me and it was where and how I see myself as well. What I’ve seen so far is that he’s so detailed. He just wants to make you better. He’s very strict, but he wants to make you a better player and that’s why I’m here.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ho has “a lot” of confidence in her, and that is hugely freeing. “That’s the part I don’t have to worry about … and I can focus on other things.”

Pelova’s experience of Tottenham had been playing against them, and the more difficult that got, the more it contributed to her decision to join. “Defending was so hard,” she says of facing Spurs last season. “So, I already liked the style Martin had the team playing. I also already know Caitlin Dijkstra; I’ve known her for eight years and we lived together in Amsterdam so we know each other so well. She’s like my sister. I know Lize Kop, they’re also one of my closest friends. So, that has made the transition easy because I can always rely on them.

“I’m quite social so I’ve been trying to get to know everyone, the youngsters. It’s quite a hard job in the beginning, it’s intense, but I like it. On the pitch, you’re building relationships, pre-season is always heavy, you just need to grind, but it has been good.”

Pelova has belief in herself and her body, too. “We train really hard. That’s different to what I’m used to. So, obviously it goes up and down, but I’m confident that in a few weeks everything as a team will have progressed so much. Always with new players, it needs time. I’ve been in football a really long time so I know how it goes.”

Asked about Tottenham’s chances of disrupting things at the top, she flips the question, then says she relishes being outsiders. “You need to put us on as underdogs. The underdog position is the place to be.”

Now, Pelova is ready for the intensity of pre-season to end and for the games to begin at home against West Ham on Sunday. One, in particular, stands out, and it comes on 25 October at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “Please, stop pre-season,” she says with a laugh. “I just want to start. I can’t wait to play against all the teams. I can’t wait to play against Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Janine Sonis: ‘63,000 fans in Denver proves a women’s team was way overdue’
Sports.content:
In the 13th minute of a 6-1 win against Chicago, Janine Sonis ran into the penalty area and stealthily positioned herself behind a line of defenders, before striking a crisp shot into the right corner. It was her ninth goal of the season, the most of any Denver Summit player, and joint-seventh in the NWSL.

Now playing for her hometown club in their debut season, the NWSL and Canada veteran feels that her happiness is translating on to the field. “I think it’s been a season that I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career, and I think that that’s showing in the way that I’m playing,” she said.

With family nearby, driving the same roads as when being driven to practice as a child, and captaining Colorado’s first women’s professional soccer team, Sonis said “it’s been, to be a little bit cliched, a dream come true to play here”, adding: “I didn’t think that Denver would get a professional women’s team while I was still playing. But it’s the 63,000 [fans at the team’s home opener at Empower Field at Mile High], the fans that continue to show up for us every week, [it] proves the point that it’s way overdue.”

The versatile 32-year-old, who is playing at left-back, has had a profound influence on their smooth transition into the league, adding a positivity to her play and a decisive impact on and off the ball in a season when many of the scorelines have been narrow. Having experienced some of the league’s growing pains, she acknowledges the progress made since its inception, leading to a moment where debutante teams such as Denver have smoother introductions.

“I think we’ve hit a point where the expectation in every environment around the NWSL is so high, especially with the CBA [collective bargaining agreement] and what the CBA requires. And so I think it’s been just really cool for me to see the evolution of the league, and then to join an expansion team and see where the floor is. I mean, with a brand new facility, building a stadium, like where teams are coming into now is just so significantly different than when I first started out.”

View image in fullscreen Janine Sonis of Denver Summit: ‘I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career.’ Photograph: Andrew Wevers/NWSL/Getty Images

Denver have spent the season looking up at the playoff positions, slowly moving up the table with a consistency of effort leading to seven wins, six draws and eight defeats, with only two losses by more than one goal. After this weekend (when Sonis also marked her 10,000th regular-season minute in the competition), the Summit are sitting just below the playoffs in ninth, with nine regular-season matches remaining.

On how to measure success for a league debutante, Sonis mentions the target of the playoffs, while noting myriad successes already achieved on and off the pitch: “It’s interesting because I think there’s two different answers. As a competitor, success to me is nothing less than making playoffs … We’re putting ourselves in incredible positions in games, we’re creating tons of opportunities, and we’re either drawing games or losing games by really small margins. I think that we have already found success in a lot of ways, and we’ve built a really clear identity and clear playing style, and have built a a solid culture in the locker room with people that are very clear about the fact that they want to be here and compete for this club.”

On what it will take to break into the playoff positions, and stay there, in an infamously chaotic and tightly packed table, Sonis said: “Our attacking relationships and the way that we create opportunities, continuing to build those partnerships in the front line. I know as a full-back, a big part of our game is getting our full-backs into the attack, so putting in quality service and helping create for those attacking players. And I think we need to be very clear that it’s one game at a time. Right now, we’re looking at it as a kind of a five-game season, and doing the most that we can in those five games to put ourselves in the best position.”

Having the Champions League winner and fellow Coloradan Lindsey Heaps on hand after she returned from playing in Europe this summer is also a boost: “I don’t think that anyone can deny when someone with that résumé and presence comes into an environment that they wouldn’t have an immediate impact on the field, but even just the culture in the locker room, her professionalism, the way that she takes care of herself, the way that she speaks, is just so influential to not just our younger players but for myself as well.”

What is Sonis’s favourite contribution of her own this season? A 94th-minute set-piece goal against the Utah Royals to secure a 2-1 win on 9 August. Of the well-rehearsed strike around the defensive wall, she said: “The free-kick was definitely special for me, just because I spend a lot of time working on them.”

Defensively, she emphasized the difficulty of defending some of the league’s elite attackers, such as Sophia Wilson: “I think my favourite thing has just been learning and getting better, and and similarly seeing the fruit of my labor and studying how to be a better defender and the art of it … I’ve been really proud of the evolution of our backline across the season, and we’ve put in so much intentional work, and it’s been really nice to see that come to life.”

Other favourite moments include games at the Colorado Rapids Stadium, where she played her state championships in high school, and, of course, setting the NWSL attendance record with 63,004 fans at Mile High Stadium. Sonis said: “I think there’s parts of it that felt like a fever dream.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 11: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Champions again at last, after a 10-year wait, Manchester City now face an even tougher task: defending their title. They appear to have a good chance of succeeding, especially after keeping their star striker, Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. The WSL’s top scorer and best player of 2025-26 performed a dramatic U-turn by signing a new four-year contract in May rather than leaving on a free transfer, and that may prove crucial in continuing City’s positive momentum.

Their squad looks to be of a similar strength to last season. The Brazil forward Kerolin left for Barcelona but Beth Mead arriving from Arsenal in essence replaces her. Similarly, the exit of left-back Leila Ouahabi will be compensated for by the acquisition of Niamh Charles from Chelsea. Perhaps the only minor question is whether there is sufficient depth to sustain a challenge in the Women’s Champions League as well as domestically, but the core of regulars looks as formidable as any club in Europe.

The team scored plenty last term and had great success down the flanks, with the right-back Kerstin Casparij providing the joint-most assists in the division. Defensively they look solid. The most intriguing challenge could be psychological, as they switch from hunters to hunted, becoming the team that everybody wants to beat. They start at home to one of the promoted sides, Birmingham City, and first meet a fellow title hopeful – Arsenal – at the start of October, when they will aim to lay down a marker in the title race.

Off-field picture

Owned by City Football Group and led off the pitch by the managing director, Charlotte O’Neill, and director of football, Therese Sjögren, City enter the season with a new women’s team building at the training centre. The £10m building offers everything from underwater treadmills to a barista-style coffee machine in the canteen, with every element tailored towards maximising performance for female athletes. Previously the women’s team sometimes had to share a gym with City’s boys’ academy.

The manager

Andrée Jeglertz’s first season could scarcely have gone better, as he oversaw a league and cup double. He arrived in Manchester after a relatively uninspiring spell in charge of Denmark women but his CV is full of extensive high-level experience, including a 2004 European title with the Swedish club Umeå. The 54-year-old is a calm presence on the touchline, unwavering in his belief that his team will “find a way to win”, and has avoided controversy in press conferences, which he handles assuredly.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead joins the champions from rivals Arsenal. Photograph: Kate Green/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

Mead was the headline signing on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. City are hoping that the England forward – the Golden Boot winner and player of the tournament at the 2022 European Championship – is not past her best, at 31, and can flourish across a three-year contract. She is the all-time leading assist provider in the WSL. Mead also has 81 caps and will want to be part of any Lionesses squad at next summer’s World Cup.

Stat attack

If teams want to defend more effectively against the champions, they could start by focusing on free-kicks and corners. City scored at least twice as many set-piece goals as anyone else in 2025-26. As strong as they were elsewhere, this was their superpower.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

The 18-year-old full-back Sacha Lewis signed her first professional contract with City in August, having been with the club since under-14 level. The younger sister of the club’s men’s first-team full-back Rico Lewis, she has been a regular for England Under-19s and has been named in the England Under-20 squad that will go to Poland for September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup. She was the player of the season for Manchester City’s “Next Gen” team last term and, with City juggling European and domestic football, may get a chance in the first team.

What they say

“Our biggest challenge this year is to continue winning and, at the same, compete in other competitions and also want to win those. Winning in one year is one thing, but being able to win in the next year, that is even tougher. Of course we can do that [compete on multiple fronts] and we have good enough players to be able to play with one starting XI on Saturday and do a couple of changes on Wednesday and still win. That was our biggest challenge last year – we had too many good players that were not playing enough games, so this year we will have the possibility to explore the whole squad. Each player will be more important than they’ve ever been for the club” – Jeglertz speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.

Where are they playing their home games?

The Joie Stadium is the women’s team’s usual home, across the road from the Etihad Stadium, where they will play two home league fixtures. Those will be against Arsenal on 4 October and against Manchester United on 14 February. The 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, that hosted matches at Euro 2022, has been the women’s team’s home for more than a decade and they were unbeaten at home in the league last season. They haven’t lost a home WSL game at the Joie Stadiumsince a 4-3 thriller against Arsenal in February 2025.

Sports.title: EFL player has contract ripped up hours before match on his birthday
Sports.content:
EFL player has contract ripped up hours before match on his birthday

Birmingham City have terminated Jack Robinson’s contract by mutual consent on what is his 33rd birthday.

The defender leaves the Blues just 12 months into a two-year deal.

3 Jack Robinson has had an eventful birthday for the second successive year Credit: Getty

Bizarrely, Robinson secured a move to St Andrews on the exact same day last year meaning he was signed and released on consecutive birthdays.

Robinson's nightmare Birmingham spell

Robinson, who signed from Sheffield United a year ago, has struggled to find his best form since arriving at the Midlands club.

He was dismissed in just his second game for the club against local rivals Coventry City.

And it got worse for the centre-back when he received another red card two games later in a league fixture against Hull City.

Things went from bad to worse for Robinson when he scored an own goal and conceded a penalty against former club Sheffield United.

Robinson represented Birmingham just 16 times in what was a lively stint at the club.

Birmingham announced his departure on X writing: “The club can confirm that Jack Robinson has left the Club following the mutual termination of his contract.

“Everyone at Blues would like to thank Jack for his efforts while at the Club and wish him well for the future.”

The decision to part ways came just hours before Birmingham Championship clash at home to Southampton, with the match finishing 1-1.

The Blues went into the match buoyed by Friday’s 2-1 win at Wrexham – their first win of the season.

3 Robinson was sent off twice within his first four games for the club Credit: Getty

3 The Blues have secured a season-long loan for Hull's Liam Millar Credit: Getty

Birmingham boss Chris Davies received some positive news during his side's clash against the Saints with the news that Liam Millar had joined the club on a season-long loan deal.

The Hull City star, who featured for Canada at this summer’s World Cup, played a key role in the Tigers’ Championship play-off triumph last season.

He made 38 appearances for Hull last season, scoring three goals and registering five assists.

The 26-year-old played in Hull’s Premier League opening weekend victory over Manchester United.

He then scored the winner in Saturday’s 1-0 win at Coventry to hand Hull maximum points from their opening two fixtures.

The Canadian has clocked up 44 caps for his country and featured in three of their five World Cup matches.

Sports.title: Man United make bonkers deadline day enquiry for Man City player
Sports.content:
Manchester United have made an audacious deadline day enquiry for Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils have been looking to strengthen at left-back all summer but to no avail, and they have now approached one of their biggest rivals just as the transfer window nears a close.

4 Rayan Ait-Nouri has been the subject of a shock approach from Man United Credit: Getty

It is understood that talks for Ait-Nouri to move across Manchester have only progressed as far as an enquiry.

Man City sources also believe that there will be no progress on a potential deal, with just hours to go until the transfer window's 11pm deadline.

Ait-Nouri has struggled for minutes since completing a £32million move to the Etihad Stadium last summer.

The Algerian made just 17 Premier League appearances for the Citizens last term following his arrival from Wolves.

He is yet to feature at all for City this season, having been on the bench for all four of their opening games, with Josko Gvardiol, Nico O’Reilly and Rico Lewis all capable of playing in the left-back role.

Man United's search for a left-back

With a shock switch to Old Trafford looking unlikely for Ait-Nouri, Man United will likely have to look elsewhere if they are to solve their left-back conundrum at the eleventh hour.

Luke Shaw is currently their only specialist in the position, and Michael Carrick's side have been unsuccessful in their attempts to land no.1 target in Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

talkSPORT recently reported that United were interested in signing Barcelona full-back Alejandro Balde as an alternative.

However, the two clubs have struggled to agree on a deal, with Barca slapping a €45million (£38.5m) asking price on the Spaniard, while the Red Devils would have preferred a loan move.

As well as Balde, United have also been credited with an interest in Fulham's Antonee Robinson and RB Leipzig defender David Raum.

4 Michael Carrick is yet to sign a left-back in his first transfer window as Man United boss Credit: Getty

4 Shaw has shouldered the bulk of United's playing demands at left-back for the past year Credit: Getty

Left-back has become a priority position for Man United this summer, with Shaw shouldering the responsibility in the role in the 2025/26 campaign.

But with Champions League football returning to Old Trafford this season, Michael Carrick will need a bigger squad to rotate.

The need to strengthen in this area was plain to see on Sunday, as Shaw struggled in United's 5-2 win over Ipswich.

Although the Red Devils won comfortably in the end, they had a scare when Leif Davis put the Tractor Boys ahead after Abdul Fatawu picked up the ball on the right and drove past Shaw to tee up the opener.

The England defender's fault in the goal drew criticism from talkSPORT's Alex Crook, who labelled him 'part of the problem' in United's backline.

Rayan Ait-Nouri's career

Though a move looks highly unlikely, Ait-Nouri would certainly offer plenty of Premier League experience at Old Trafford.

4 Ait-Nouri built a strong reputation for himself whilst at Wolves Credit: Getty

The 25-year-old broke into senior football with Angers in France, before signing with Wolves on an initial loan deal in 2020, before making the move permanent a year later.

He made 135 league appearances at Molineux before making the switch to the Etihad.

While he struggled for minutes at club level last season, he impressed at the World Cup, where he featured for Algeria as they reached the Round of 32 before being knocked out by Switzerland.

Despite being born in France, he has been capped 34 times by the North African nation.

Sports.title: Ben Chilwell could make shock Premier League return in deadline day move out of nowhere
Sports.content:
Ben Chilwell could make shock Premier League return in deadline day move out of nowhere

Crystal Palace are exploring a move for ex-Chelsea defender Ben Chilwell, talkSPORT understands.

The England left-back joined BlueCo-owned Strasbourg on Transfer Deadline Day last year, having fallen out of favour at Stamford Bridge.



4 Chilwell provided two assists in 20 Ligue 1 appearances for Strasbourg last term Credit: Getty

Chilwell penned a two-year deal with the Ligue 1 side last year, almost a year on from his last appearance for Chelsea.

The defender was frozen out by former Blues boss Enzo Maresca, and spent the second half of the 2024/25 season on loan at Crystal Palace.

Familiar face

Palace now appear to be keen on bringing Chilwell back to Selhurst Park for a second spell.



talkSPORT understands the Eagles want to complete a late Deadline Day switch for the 29-year-old.

Despite their interest, is not currently clear if the Premier League outfit are considering a loan or a permanent move for Chilwell.



Palace's interest in the defender comes as they continue to assess their options ahead of the end of the transfer window.

The south London outfit have been in a period of transition this summer, with Pierre Sage taking over from Oliver Glasner in the dugout.



They have had to deal with major departures too, with Maxence Lacroix moved to Chelsea in a deal worth £52million, before Daniel Munoz left to join Glasner at Nottingham Forest.

Palace have strengthened their back line by bringing in proven Premier League experience in Takehiro Tomiyasu and Axel Disasi.

But after losing their opening two league games under Sage, they could now look to bolster their ranks further by making a late play for Chilwell.

4 Chilwell scored once in his 2025 loan spell at Crystal Palace



4 New Crystal Palace boss could be keen on bringing in more Premier League experience by snapping up Chilwell Credit: Getty

During his loan spell at the club in 2025, he made 11 appearances and completed a Premier League game just once.

Ben Chilwell's career

Should Chilwell seal a return to Selhurst Park, it would see him come back to English football after just a year at Strasbourg.

The Leicester academy graduate was one of six players to depart Chelsea to join their Ligue 1 sister club last summer, as he was convinced to join the club by then manager Liam Rosenior.



He enjoyed a resurgence campaign at Strasbourg, making 34 appearances in all competitions - his most since the 2020/21 season.

Chilwell also played a significant role in Strasbourg's historic Conference League run, featuring nine times as they reached their first ever European semi-final before being beaten by Rayo Vallecano in the last four.

The defender first made a name for himself at Leicester, as he graduated from the club's youth ranks to become a highly-rated left-back in the Premier League.

4 Chilwell has finally departed Chelsea last year, having been deemed as surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge Credit: PA



He made 123 appearances for the Foxes, scoring four goals, and made his senior England debut in 2018 whilst at the club.

In 2020, Chilwell joined Chelsea in a deal worth up to £50million, penning a five year deal.

His first season at Stamford Bridge was his most successful, as he featured 43 times in all competitions - including playing ten games in the Blues' victorious Champions League campaign.

However, Chilwell's time in west London was hampered by injuries, which caused him to miss 110 games in his five years at the club.



The arrival of Enzo Maresca as head coach in the summer of 2024 all but spelled the end of his Chelsea career, as he played just once under the Italian in the Carabao Cup before leaving to join Palace on loan, with his permanent exit following last summer.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun’s £40m Everton move collapse sees Chelsea capitalise as they resurrect deal
Sports.content:
Folarin Balogun's expected failed move to Everton has opened the door for Monaco teammate Lamine Camara to join Chelsea.

The west London club have agreed a deal to sign Camara for a fixed €55million (£47m).



3 Camara's move to Chelsea has come as a result of Folarin Balogun's collapsed transfer Credit: Getty

The combative midfielder has signed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge with the option of an additional 12 months.

It is understood that the deal was personally driven by Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali.

In a frantic end to deadline day, the Camara deal was looking all but off but doubts over Balogun's move to Everton left Monaco sweating over a much-needed sale.



Chelsea quickly took advantage of Monaco precarious position and swooped in to bolster their midfield ahead of Enzo Fernandez's move to Manchester City.

USA international Balogun, appeared primed to complete a deadline day switch to the Toffees but an issue spotted at his medical threw the deal into jeopardy.



The Ligue 1 leaders' deadline day plans were plunged into chaos with Monaco needing to sell players to balance the books.

It is understood that Monaco had a replacement lined up for Balogun.

Camara has attracted interest from the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool, with the Blues having led the race to sign the Senegal international this summer.



David Moyes' side have been in the market for a new presence up top, with Beto joining Italian club Fiorentina.

And Balogun was eyed as the ideal candidate, especially given his previous experience of English football.

3 Balogun's Premier League return may be on hold in a dramatic turn of events Credit: Getty

Balogun's Arsenal career

Balogun came through Arsenal's famed academy and went on to make ten first team appearances for the club, including two in the Premier League.



However, it wasn't until the 2022/23 campaign when Balogun truly broke out as he scored 22 goals while on loan at French outfit Reims.

Balogun's haul prompted Monaco to sign him for an initial £25.7million in August 2023.

The ex-Gunners prodigy has since netted 31 goals in 91 appearances across all competitions for Monaco and was named their Player of the Season for the 2025/26 campaign.

Folarin Balogun became a lightning rod for controversy at the World Cup

Balogun also found himself at the centre of a political storm during this summer's World Cup.



He was sent off for the United States during their Round of 32 contest against Bosnia, which the co-hosts won 2-0.

3 Balogun's red card created one of the biggest storylines during the World Cup Credit: Getty

The red card meant Balogun picked up a one-match suspension, which ruled him out of the USMNT's Round of 16 clash with Belgium.

However, Balogun's ban was controversially overturned following intervention from United States president Donald Trump.



Balogun's return ultimately mattered little as Belgium romped to a 4-1 win.

Sports.title: Leeds avoid transfer nightmare with minutes to spare as they agree deal to sign highly-rated winger
Sports.content:
Leeds avoid transfer nightmare with minutes to spare as they agree deal to sign highly-rated winger

Leeds United have agreed a deal to sign Eintracht Frankfurt attacker Jean-Matteo Bahoya, talkSPORT understands.

The France Under-21 international will head to Elland Road on an initial loan deal with an obligation to buy, with Leeds winger Wilfried Gnonto set to depart the club and join Fiorentina.



3 Bahoya swaps the Bundesliga for the Premier League Credit: Getty

This represents a dramatic late turnaround, after it initially appeared as though Gnonto would not be allowed to leave.

The 22-year-old had spent the past 24 hours in Italy in the hope of completing a move to Fiorentina, with pictures of him in their iconic purple kit circulating on social media.

However, talkSPORT previously reported that Leeds wouldn't sanction a deal for Gnonto without finding a replacement.



But with the Whites since agreeing a deal to sign Bahoya in his place, this has paved the way for Gnonto to join Fiorentina.

Late drama

Leeds now look set to prevail in the race to sign Frankfurt star Bahoya, who has been chased by several Premier League clubs this summer.



Sunderland have also enquired about the 21-year-old, while Hull previously came closest to securing his signature.

The Tigers had agreed a deal to sign Bahoya, with permission granted for a medical, only for the player to turn down the transfer.



But a move to England in the final few hours of the transfer window is now set to materialise, with Leeds the destination.

A deal for Bahoya has been triggered as Gnonto closes in on a move to Fiorentina at the 11th hour.

The transfer appears close to completion, with talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs reporting that Gnonto had completed his medical with the Serie A outfit.

3 WGnonto has been a fan favourite at Elland Road over the last four years Credit: Getty



Gnonto's imminent move away from Elland Road will spell the end of his four-year stay at the club.

Since joining the Whites in 2022, the Italy international has made 147 appearances, scoring 23 times. He played a key role in the club's promotion back to the Premier League in 2025.

Who is Jean-Matteo Bahoya?

A France U21 international, Bahoya earned Premier League interest after impressing over the last two years at Frankfurt.

The 21-year-old joined the Bundesliga side from French club Angers in 2024, and has since registered seven goals and eight assists in 78 outings.



With Bahoya's preferred position on the left wing, he is capable of playing in various attacking positions, and would serve as a like-for-like replacement for Gnonto.

He offers blistering pace, having set a Bundesliga speed record after being clocked at 23.09mph during a match against Bochum in 2025.

3 Leeds are set to sign the Bundesliga's fastest-ever player in Bahoya Credit: Getty

Leeds' pursuit of Bahoya also follows their failure to land Mykhailo Mudryk, who is set to join Tottenham on loan.



Should Bahoya join Leeds, he will become their sixth signing of the summer transfer window, which has seen them complete the record-breaking signing of goalkeeper James Trafford, while Harry Wilson has also moved to Elland Road from Fulham.

Sports.title: Jurrien Timber’s brother Quinten could join Premier League club in late move
Sports.content:
Quinten Timber’s hopes of a dream Premier League switch hinge on the final hours of the transfer window.

The Marseille midfielder could join Crystal Palace but the Eagles are against the clock to get the deal done before the deadline.



3 Quinten and Jurrien Timber have both earned caps for the Netherlands Credit: Getty

Should Palace get the deal over the line, it would see him join Arsenal full-back and twin brother Jurrien in English football.

Timber has been tipped for a move to the Premier League since his brother’s move to the Emirates Stadium three years ago.

The Dutchman, who impressed for the Ligue 1 giants last season, is the subject of a £17million bid from Palace.



The south London club were not the only possible suitors this summer with FC Porto and Aston Villa have also been credited with an interest in him.

The Netherlands international arrived at Marseille in January following a three-and-a-half year spell with Feyenoord.



However, due to the club's tumultuous financial situation, Marseille need to offload their saleable assets to balance the books.

Marseille have already offloaded former Arsenal and Chelsea striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.



They were also forced to sell ex-Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood to Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

Marseille boss Manager Bruno Genesio made clear his intention to hold onto Timber and it appears that he is not going to get his wish.

Long-standing interest

The 25-year-old first attracted interest from Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham back in 2023.

3 Timber has made a big impression since joining Marseille in January Credit: Getty



3 The 25-year-old featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup Credit: AFP

But a move to the Premier League failed to materialise prior to his move to the Stade Velodrome.

He clocked up 15 appearances for Marseille, helping the club to a fifth-placed finish in Ligue 1.

Despite swapping his homeland for Ligue 1 midway through the season, Timber was included in the Netherlands squad for the World Cup.



But his hopes of accompanying his brother in the squad this summer were dashed when Jurrien withdrew from the squad through injury just days before the tournament.

Timber is now expected to leave cash-strapped Marseille either on Tuesday night or January at the earliest.

He was handed his first start of the season in Sunday’s 2-0 defeat at Ligue 1 leaders Monaco.

Sports.title: Martin Keown explains why Arsenal do not need to make any more signings despite Gabriel Martinelli exit
Sports.content:
Martin Keown explains why Arsenal do not need to make any more signings despite Gabriel Martinelli exit

Martin Keown believes Max Dowman's omission from Arsenal's squad against Aston Villa proves they have enough firepower to compete.

Dowman, who plays as a forward, was not involved in the Gunners' 1-0 win over Villa on Monday evening.



3 Dowman was on the bench for the Community Shield and Arsenal's Premier League opener against Coventry Credit: Getty

Instead, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta opted for Eberechi Eze, Viktor Gyokeres and Noni Madueke as his attacking options on the bench.

Even then, Eze was the only member of the trio who came on against Villa, although the nature of the contest after Bukayo Saka's 59th-minute strike meant a more controlled approach was required.

However, there will come a time when Arteta needs to lean on the full range of attackers in the squad.



Which attacking players have left Arsenal this summer, and who has joined?

Worryingly, Arsenal look set to end the transfer window short on forwards as Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard have both exited while Gabriel Martinelli is on the verge of joining Al Hilal for a club record figure.

Teenage star Ethan Nwaneri has also departed on loan to Borussia Dortmund.



In contrast, Christos Tszolis is the Gunners' sole attacking acquisition this summer.

Despite the imbalance in numbers, Keown believes it will be enough for Arsenal to defend their Premier League crown.



Martin Keown's verdict on Arsenal's depth

"I'm comfortable with the group," Keown said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Yes, numerically you need another wide player.

"But Max Dowman is a young player that couldn't even get on the bench, such is the quality of that group."

Keown also felt Dowman's exclusion gave weight to Arteta's push for larger Premier League matchday squads.

3 Any injuries to attacking players could have Arteta sweating nervously Credit: Getty



In the Premier League, teams can name up to 20 players for games.

It is a noticeably lower figure compared to other leading European leagues, as LaLiga clubs can name 23 players in their matchday squads while Serie A allows for 25.

"Maybe that's (larger matchday squads) something that needs to come in because one or two of these guys can't sit on the bench," Keown said.

Who has Arsenal attempted to sign this summer?

Should Arteta get his wish, he won't have a lengthy list of alternative attacking options to call on.

But it hasn't been for a lack of trying.

3 Arsenal could not turn their dream of signing Vini Jr a reality Credit: AFP



Arsenal targeted Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, but neither pursuit was successful.

Rogers instead joined Chelsea for £117million while Vini Jr inked a new deal to remain at Real Madrid.

Belgian forward Malick Fofana was also offered to the Gunners but they chose not to pursue the deal with Fofana heading to Sunderland.

Sports.title: Man City agree Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals with no replacement incoming
Sports.content:
Manchester City have struck a £125million deadline-day deal to secure Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, with Enzo Maresca finally set to land his top target from his former employers. It equals the British transfer record which was paid to Newcastle by Liverpool for Alexander Isak last summer, and is a fixed fee for the 25-year-old Argentinian with no add-ons involved. While Chelsea reached an agreement which took their incomings towards the £500m mark for the summer – with club sources pointing out that is also a British record – they did so without having their own replacement at the ready. However, with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, Chelsea dramatically agreed a deal with Monaco for their midfielder Lamine Camara worth £47m. That breakthrough followed Monaco's proposed sale of Folarin Balogun to Everton meeting last-minute complications. Chelsea had already seen two bids worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down for Camara earlier in the day. They remained in a race against the clock before the 11pm deadline. City leaving their club-to-club negotiations until the final two days of the window had left Chelsea with limited time to secure their own signing. Manchester City have reached an agreement with Chelsea for the signing of Enzo Fernandez Central to Chelsea agreeing to a deal with City was Fernandez’s relationship with Maresca with the two wanting to work together again. Fernandez was known to have been keen to leave, having flirted with that idea before the last season had even finished. With no Fernandez – and with Dario Essugo joining Strasbourg on loan – Chelsea’s senior midfield options are Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson. Malo Gusto can also be used centrally if required. While Fernandez developed a helpful habit of scoring important goals, Xabi Alonso has an impressive attack, having signed Morgan Rogers for £117m this summer to form a front three with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Chelsea fans may be glad that what turned into an exhausting saga is coming to an end at least. Chelsea initially attempted to accelerate a conclusion by creating their own deadline for bids by Friday August 14 at 5pm. That was for a £120m transfer and the terms were communicated to their Premier League counterparts via Fernandez’s camp, led by Javier Pastore. Chelsea’s hope was that it would give them ample time to replace their 2022 World Cup-winning midfielder. However, City did not play along with Chelsea’s deadline. No offer was submitted, and Blues insiders claimed they ‘expected’ Fernandez to stay with them for the entirety of 2026-27. He was even handed the captain’s armband when he appeared as a substitute in their final friendly at home to Real Sociedad, receiving a mixed reception inside Stamford Bridge. Fernandez appeared in their Premier League opener at Fulham as a substitute. While the home fans inside Craven Cottage booed him after Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup, the away end welcomed him warmly, with those Chelsea supporters even chanting his name. Fernandez continued to train with his team-mates and in Alonso’s main squad rather than the second group including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, but then disappeared. Following talks with Alonso, he was not involved in their Carabao Cup win over Luton, or in their Premier League victory against Brighton. Alonso insisted publicly it was his decision after speaking with the player, but did add he selected a squad that had the ‘desire to play’. Maresca had a good relationship with Fernandez at Chelsea, where he often wore the captain’s armband in the absence of James. Maresca also handed him that armband barely a month after the Argentinian was accused of singing a racist song following his country’s 2024 Copa America triumph. That was in Chelsea’s Premier League opener at home to City. When Maresca eventually exited Chelsea after speaking with City about succeeding Pep Guardiola, Fernandez was among those who spoke up, suggesting it ‘hurt’ the team. The Blues ended up finishing 10th in that season, leaving them with no European football under Alonso for this term. Sports.title: Tony Romo opens up on private alcohol struggles leading up to drunk-driving arrest as he pleads no contest to charges... and reveals if he plans to return to CBS NFL booth
Sports.content:
NFL legend and CBS analyst Tony Romo candidly opened up on his struggles with pain medication and alcohol dependency as he pleaded no contest over his drunk-driving arrest.

Romo, 46, was pulled over in his Jeep in Milwaukee on July 23 and later charged with OWI after performing poorly in sobriety tests, with humiliating bodycam footage of the incident quickly going viral.

Over a month on from the arrest, the former quarterback took accountability for his action as he pleaded no contest to the offense.

'Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life,' he said in a statement on Tuesday. 'I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting.

'Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better.

'This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me.

NFL legend and CBS analyst Tony Romo pleaded no contest to an OWI charge

The former quarterback was arrested after being pulled over in Milwaukee on July 23

'This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWl in Wisconsin. I own this completely.'

The former Dallas Cowboys star also opened up on his private health battles as he addressed his future with CBS.

Romo revealed that he had been struggling with a dependency on pain medication after multiple back surgeries during his playing career left him in debilitating pain. He said that he turned to alcohol in an effort to wean himself off the medication.

'Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain,' he added. 'That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.

'As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward.

'That path requires honesty.

'None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them.'

Romo was placed on indefinite leave by CBS following his arrest and temporarily replaced by JJ Watt and the future of his $18m-a-year CBS contract has been shrouded in doubt.

Romo has been on leave at CBS since his OWI arrest month in his native Wisconsin

Yet, Romo appeared to hint that he would eventually return to the booth after taking time away to focus on his health.

'The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant,; he continued.

'It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully - to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public.

'I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.

'As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.'

Court records show Romo reached a deal with prosecutors on Tuesday to close out the case.

His driving privileges have been revoked for six months and was ordered to attend and complete an alcohol assessment program. Additionally, an ignition interlock device must be installed on his cars for the next year.

Romo was also ordered to pay a $784 fine, records stated.

Romo was on his way home from a golf tournament in Milwaukee when he was pulled over by cops last month, telling them he had not had anything to drink and was on his way to visit 'Grandma and Grandpa'.

A police report later revealed that an officer found an 'open bottle of an alcoholic beverage' on the passenger side of his black Jeep vehicle.

A week on from his arrest, CBS placed him on leave and Romo has been keeping a low profile ever since.

The NFL quarterback legend poses for a photo with his wife Candice at a 2023 golf tournament

CBS Sports president David Berson, meanwhile, spoke to the media ahead of the NFL season and confirmed that the network has no immediate plans for Romo to return to TV screens.

'It's an evolving situation and therefore we are still assessing,' he said on August 11. 'There is no timetable or final decision at this time.

'I hope you can respect and appreciate this is a personnel matter and a legal one for Tony, so I can't speak to that aspect of things.'

Romo is owed $72m over the next four years of his current contract, putting the network in a precarious position as they decide what to do next.

On the air, Romo's work as the lead color analyst for the NFL on CBS has become increasingly divisive with fans.

As he approaches what would be his 10th season with the network, he has been facing calls to step down after being criticized for his strange affectations and errors in commentary.

Whether it was confusing Josh Allen for Patrick Mahomes , letting out a bizarre groan during the Bills-Jaguars game or calling a 4th & 1 carry like a first-down , Romo had his share of blunders in last season's playoffs alone.

Romo, who famously dated Jessica Simpson, is married to wife Candice, a past Miss Missouri

Romo said he felt unwell during the Bills-Jaguars incident, explaining: 'We had a bunch of guys sick, we were just grinding through it. You’re not going to miss a playoff game.'

In December 2023, at the height of 'Tayvis' Mania, Romo bizarrely addressed Taylor Swift as the wife of Travis Kelce while she watched him play for the Kansas City Chiefs.

It came long before the couple announced their engagement back in August of 2025 and got married last month.

Romo, who famously dated Jessica Simpson from 2007 to 2009, is married to Candice Crawford Romo, a former broadcast journalist and past Miss Missouri. They have three children.

Sports.title: Man City complete £65m signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton - as Enzo Maresca's side beat Tottenham to forward's signature
Sports.content:
Man City complete £65m signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton - as Enzo Maresca's side beat Tottenham to forward's signature

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City have completed the signing of winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton.

The Senegal forward has joined Enzo Maresca's side in a deal worth _, bringing an end to his two-year stay on Merseyside.

City have beaten Tottenham to the forward's signature, after Roberto De Zerbi and Co had agreed terms with Everton.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Tottenham opened discussions last week when it became apparent that Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo would opt to join Manchester City should the Anfield club agree to sell.

Ndiaye has turned down multiple contract offers in the last 12 months.

He scored 17 goals and provided four assists in 74 appearances for Everton, since joining in a £15m move from Marseille in 2024.

Manchester City have beaten Tottenham to the signing of winger Iliman Ndiaye

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi had been appointed as Marseille's head coach just days before Ndiaye was sold, with the winger never playing a match under the Italian.

Ndiaye, who has 44 caps for Senegal, had previously been an integral to Sheffield United's Championship promotion season in 2023.

Richarlison had been set to return to the Toffees from Tottenham in a near-swap deal for Ndiaye, but that stalled and City pounced.

Everton, meanwhile, are set to re-sign Jack Grealish from City as his replacement.

Ndiaye could go straight into the City team to face Coventry this weekend, with Jeremy Doku out injured.
